# 📅 **Dollywood Timeline Map: Key Events & Transitions**

This visual timeline traces the evolution of Dollywood from its founding to 2018, highlighting major **name changes**, **ownership shifts**, **park expansions**, **ride additions**, and **cultural milestones**. Each transition is clearly marked with **year, location, significance**, and **context** to reinforce chronological understanding and memory.

---

## 🚀 Founding & Early Years (1961–1975)

| Year | Event | Location | Significance |
|------|------|--------|-------------|
| **1961** | Opened as **Rebel Railroad** | Pigeon Forge, TN | Founded by Robbins brothers; themed around Civil War; included steam train, saloon, blacksmith shop, general store. Modeled after their successful Tweetsie Railroad. |
| **1964** | Renamed **Goldrush Junction** | Pigeon Forge, TN | Shifted to a Wild West theme; aligned with sister park Tweetsie Railroad. Announced in *Knoxville News Sentinel*. |
| **1970** | Purchased by **Art Modell** (Cleveland Browns owner) | Pigeon Forge, TN | Park retained railroad; added outdoor theater and Robert F. Thomas Chapel. |
| **1975** | Renamed **Goldrush** | Pigeon Forge, TN | Simplified name; continued as a Wild West-themed park. |

> 🔁 **Transition Summary**: *Rebel Railroad → Goldrush Junction → Goldrush*  
> **Theme Shift**: Civil War → Wild West  
> **Ownership**: Robbins → Art Modell

---

## 🏢 Ownership & Rebranding (1976–1986)

| Year | Event | Location | Significance |
|------|------|--------|-------------|
| **1976** | Purchased by **Jack & Pete Herschend** (owners of Silver Dollar City) | Pigeon Forge, TN | Park operated as **Goldrush** through 1976. Herschends invested $1M in upgrades. |
| **1977** | Renamed **Silver Dollar City Tennessee** | Pigeon Forge, TN | Became sister park to Silver Dollar City in Branson, MO. Added two new steam locomotives (#70, #71). |

> 🔁 **Transition Summary**: *Goldrush → Silver Dollar City Tennessee*  
> **Ownership**: Art Modell → Herschend  
> **Theme**: Wild West → Stronger regional identity (Tennessee)  
> **Key Addition**: Steam locomotives from White Pass & Yukon Route

---

## 🎵 Dolly Parton’s Entry & Rebranding to Dollywood (1986–1990)

| Year | Event | Location | Significance |
|------|------|--------|-------------|
| **1986** | Reopened as **Dollywood** on May 3 | Pigeon Forge, TN | Dolly Parton bought interest in park; rebranded to reflect her roots and Smoky Mountain heritage. First season attendance **doubled to over 1 million**. |
| **1986** | New Rivertown Junction area opened | Pigeon Forge, TN | Included: Smoky Mountain River Rampage, Back Porch Theater, Aunt Granny’s Dixie Fixins’, Dolly’s Tennessee Mountain Home (childhood cabin replica), and *Rags to Riches: The Dolly Parton Story* museum. |
| **1987** | **Daydream Ridge** opened | Pigeon Forge, TN | Added: Mountain Slidewinder, Mountain Dan’s Burger House, Sweet Dreams Candy Shop, Rainbow Factory, Critter Creek Playground. Engine #70 restored. |
| **1988** | **1,739-seat Celebrity Theater** opened | Pigeon Forge, TN | Hosted *Showcase of Stars* concert series. |
| **1989** | **Thunder Express** opened | Pigeon Forge, TN | Steel mine train coaster relocated from Six Flags Over Mid-America. Last season for National Mountain Music Festival. |

> 🔁 **Transition Summary**: *Silver Dollar City Tennessee → Dollywood*  
> **Ownership**: Herschend → Dolly Parton (partial ownership)  
> **Theme**: Wild West → Smoky Mountain culture  
> **Key Additions**: Dolly’s childhood home, music museum, major rides, concert venue

---
